Nematode growth medium (NGM) plates (see Recipes) LB broth (see Recipes) OP50-1 culture (see Recipes) Recipes Nematode growth medium (NGM) plates Prepare 3 g of sodium chloride, 2.5 g of peptone, and 25 g of agar in 970 mL of water, then autoclave the solution (15 psi pressure at 121 °C for 30–60 min) to sterilize it. Once the solution has reached a bearable temperature (bearable when the container touches the ventral side of the arm below the hand), add 25 mL of potassium phosphate buffer and 1 mL each of 1 M magnesium sulfate, 1 M calcium chloride, cholesterol, streptomycin, and nystatin in a laminar flow hood. After thorough mixing, pour 25 mL of the solution into 10 cm Petri plates and allow it to cool inside the laminar flow hood overnight and solidify. Spread 500 µL of 5× concentrated OP50-1 bacterial culture on the NGM plates and incubate at 37 °C for 16 h. After 16 h, store the plates at 4 °C until used. Although the plates can be stored at 4 °C for a month if properly stored in a sealed box with reduced perspiration, use the plates within a week. LB broth Dissolve 25 g of LB in 1 L of water in a 5 L conical flask and autoclave to sterilize the media. The autoclaved LB media can be stored at 4 °C for up to a month or until its sterility is compromised by outside contaminants. OP50-1 culture Inoculate a colony of the OP50-1 E. coli strain in LB broth (1 L of LB broth prepared as in Recipe

containing streptomycin sulfate (working concentration of 100 μg/mL) using a sterile inoculating loop. OP50-1 obtained from CGC should be cultured, maintained, and stored at -80 °C. Streak the OP50-1 in an LB agar plate to isolate a single colony (refer to basic microbiological technique for maintenance of bacterial strain). Incubate the culture at 37 °C at 250 rpm in a bacterial incubator (shaking the culture at 250 rpm improves oxygenation, resulting in better bacterial growth) for 16 h. After 16 h, concentrate the bacterial culture five times by centrifugation at 4,000× g for 10 min in a 50 mL tube; remove the necessary supernatant (40 mL). Vortex (use maximum speed setting in the vortexer) the pellet to disperse the bacterial pellet, which can then be used to spread on the NGM plates (500 μL of bacterial culture/NGM plate). steps.title: Gather materials, reagents, and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect the following biological materials: C. elegans strains (N2 wild‑type and glod‑4 mutant) from CGC (Minneapolis, USA) or NBRP (Tokyo, Japan). Obtain E. coli OP50‑1 from CGC. Prepare reagents with catalog numbers: Sodium chloride (Sigma S9888), Bacto™ peptone (BD 211677), Agar (BD DIFCO 214510), Calcium chloride (Sigma C3881), Magnesium sulfate (Sigma 208094), Cholesterol (Sigma C8667), Streptomycin sulfate (Sigma S1567), Nystatin (Chem Impex 00816), Potassium phosphate monobasic (Sigma P0662), Potassium phosphate dibasic (Sigma P3786), LB broth (BD Difco 244610), Serotonin hydrochloride (Sigma H9523). Make solutions: 1 M CaCl₂ (autoclave), 1 M MgSO₄ (autoclave), 5 mg/mL cholesterol in ethanol, 100 mg/mL streptomycin sulfate (0.2 µm filter), 10 mg/mL nystatin in ethanol, potassium phosphate buffer (mix 868 mL 1 M monobasic + 132 mL 1 M dibasic, pH 6, autoclave), 0.5 M serotonin HCl stock. Use double‑distilled or MilliQ water unless otherwise noted. Gather laboratory supplies: 5 L glass conical flasks, 1 000 mL and 500 mL measuring cylinders, spatula, disposable pipettes (50 mL, 25 mL, 10 mL) with motorized controller (Accuhelp PH01‑B), micropipette tips and Eppendorf pipette, 10 cm sterile plastic Petri dishes (Celltreat 229695), inoculating loop (UltraCruz sc‑200265).

steps.title: Prepare NGM agar plates
steps.instruction: In a 5 L conical flask, combine 970 mL water, 3 g sodium chloride, 2.5 g Bacto™ peptone, and 25 g agar. Autoclave at 15 psi, 121 °C for 30–60 min. After cooling to a temperature that can be safely touched, add 25 mL potassium phosphate buffer (pH 6), then add 1 mL each of 1 M MgSO₄, 1 M CaCl₂, 5 mg/mL cholesterol in ethanol, 100 mg/mL streptomycin sulfate (filter‑sterilized), and 10 mg/mL nystatin in ethanol. Mix thoroughly in a laminar flow hood. Pour 25 mL of the molten agar into each 10 cm Petri plate; let plates solidify overnight in the hood. Spread 500 µL of 5× concentrated OP50‑1 culture onto each plate, then incubate at 37 °C for 16 h. After incubation, store plates at 4 °C (stable up to 1 month if sealed, but use within 1 week).

substeps.instruction: Make potassium phosphate buffer (868 mL 1 M monobasic + 132 mL 1 M dibasic, pH 6) and autoclave.
Pour 25 mL per 10 cm plate and solidify.
Seed plates with 500 µL OP50‑1 culture and incubate.

steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Dissolve 25 g LB powder in 1 L double‑distilled water inside a 5 L conical flask. Autoclave to sterilize. Store the sterile LB broth at 4 °C for up to 1 month or until sterility is compromised.

steps.title: Prepare OP50‑1 bacterial culture
steps.instruction: Streak OP50‑1 from the stock onto an LB agar plate and isolate a single colony. Inoculate that colony into 1 L LB broth containing streptomycin sulfate to a final concentration of 100 µg/mL. Incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm for 16 h. Centrifuge the culture at 4,000×g for 10 min in a 50 mL tube; discard 40 mL supernatant, leaving the bacterial pellet. Vortex the pellet at maximum speed to resuspend. Use 500 µL of this concentrated culture to seed each NGM plate.

steps.title: Synchronize worm embryos
steps.instruction: On fresh NGM plates seeded with OP50‑1, place 35 young‑adult hermaphrodite worms per plate. Incubate at 20 °C for 30 min to allow egg laying. Remove the adult worms (discard or keep for other use). Continue incubating the plates at 20 °C until the embryos develop to the young‑adult stage, approximately 65 h after the timed egg‑laying.

steps.title: Apply drug treatment
steps.instruction: For a 5 mM serotonin treatment, overlay each NGM plate with 250 µL of a 500 mM serotonin hydrochloride stock solution. Rotate the plate to spread the liquid evenly across the agar surface. Allow the solution to air‑dry in the laminar flow hood so it diffuses into the agar, achieving the desired final concentration. For control plates, add an equal volume of water. After drying, incubate the worms on the treated plates for the specified duration (e.g., 1 h for serotonin, 24 h for MG‑H1).

substeps.instruction: Overlay plate with 250 µL 500 mM serotonin stock.

steps.title: Transfer worms to assay plates
steps.instruction: Move 30–40 synchronized young‑adult worms onto each treatment or control plate. Ensure worms are placed on the bacterial lawn. Incubate for the appropriate period before recording (e.g., 1 h after serotonin exposure).

steps.title: Record pharyngeal pumping
steps.instruction: Set up a stereomicroscope (e.g., Leica M165 FC) with a 2× objective, bright‑field illumination, and a camera. Adjust camera exposure to ~5 ms per frame. Place the assay plate on a transparent OHP sheet to facilitate smooth movement. Choose a healthy, actively moving worm on the bacterial lawn; avoid injured or immobile worms and worms outside the lawn. Keep the worm in the field of view by moving the plate (or OHP sheet) as needed. Record a 40‑second video of the worm’s pharyngeal activity. Use eyelash picks if gentle transfer of worms is required.
